carousels.name: 5 conversations couples should have about p*rn (1,755 couples)

slides.title: 5 conversations couples should have [[about p*rn.]]
slides.sub: When partners' use differs, relationships tend to struggle.

slides.title: Couples [[studied]]
slides.body: In a study of 1,755 couples (Willoughby et al., 2016), bigger differences in partners' p*rn use were linked to lower relationship satisfaction, less positive communication and more conflict. The gap matters — so talk about it.

slides.title: Talk [[1–2]]
items: "What does p*rn mean to you?" Harmless, hurtful, cheating?
"How do you feel about it in our relationship?"

slides.title: Talk [[3–5]]
items: "Has it ever made you feel compared?"
"What would honesty look like for us?"
"How can we support each other?"

slides.title: How to [[start]]
items: Pick a calm moment, not right after a fight.
Listen more than you defend.
No interrogations — curiosity, not blame.
Come back to it — one talk isn't enough.
slides.note: Send this to your partner and talk tonight ↗

slides.title:
Talk openly.
[[Heal together.]]
slides.lead: RezenIt offers habit tracking your partner can see, 1-on-1 accountability and a guided p*rn recovery program.

carousels.name: 4 body signals a p*rn urge is coming

slides.title: 4 body signals [[a p*rn urge is coming.]]
slides.sub: Your body often knows before your brain admits it.

slides.title: [[Restless]] hands
slides.body: Tapping, fidgeting, picking up your phone for no reason. Many people say this shows up minutes before a p*rn urge.

slides.title: A [[glazed]] scroll
slides.body: Thumb moving, eyes not really reading. That's autopilot — and autopilot drifts toward p*rn.

slides.title: Signals [[3–4]]
items: Tight chest or shallow breathing — stress building up.
Heavy, tired body late at night, but you won't go to bed.

slides.title: When you [[notice]]
items: Name it: "That's the signal."
Stand up and change rooms.
Breathe slowly — 4 in, 6 out, five times.
Put the phone face-down, out of reach.
slides.note: Which signal shows up first for you? Comment 1–4 👇

slides.title:
Catch it early.
[[RezenIt helps.]]
slides.lead: A panic button with instant tools, guided audio for stress and journaling to learn your signals.

carousels.name: 3 reasons 'I'm not ready to quit p*rn' is a lie (harsh)

slides.title: 3 reasons "I'm just not ready to quit p*rn" [[is a lie you tell yourself.]]
slides.sub: Ready is a feeling. Quitting is a decision.

slides.title: Ready [[never]] comes
slides.body: Life won't hand you a calm, perfect month. Waiting to feel ready is how years of p*rn pass.

slides.title: You're [[scared]], not unready
slides.body: Scared of failing. Scared of who you are without p*rn. Fear is normal. It's not a reason.

slides.title: You [[like]] the excuse
slides.body: "Not ready" lets you keep watching without feeling like you've given up. It's a pause button on guilt.

slides.title: Decide [[instead]]
items: Pick a start date within 7 days.
Write your reason in one sentence.
Block p*rn on one device today.
Tell someone the date.
slides.note: Been "not ready" for a while? Comment your start date 👇

slides.title:
Stop waiting.
[[Start with RezenIt.]]
slides.lead: A step-by-step p*rn recovery program, a blocker and accountability so you can start before you feel ready.

carousels.name: 5 clues your reason for dropping p*rn is now your own (NNN)

slides.title: 5 clues your reason for dropping p*rn [[is now yours, not the challenge's.]]
slides.sub: 5 days left. What happens after matters more.

slides.title: Clues [[1–2]]
items: You're not counting down to Dec 1.
You'd keep going even if nobody knew.

slides.title: Clues [[3–4]]
items: You care about why you watched p*rn, not just whether.
You've changed your setup — phone, nights, people.

slides.title: You like [[who you're becoming]]
slides.body: Not perfect. Just more honest, more present, more in control. That's worth more than any challenge badge.

slides.title: If that's [[you]]
items: Set a goal that has nothing to do with November.
Keep the routines that got you here.
Tell someone you're done with p*rn for good.
Be proud — quietly.
